title: Expose Toolkit CPT fields through Elementor dynamic tags
description: Add a Toolkit-owned Elementor dynamic tag so Filter Controller field bindings can select managed CPT fields instead of relying only on manual keys.
objective: Make the field binding path practical: the widget can select Toolkit CPT meta/taxonomy fields through Elementor dynamic tags, and the runtime can read public Toolkit meta values for public posts.
inputs_required: local Elementor dynamic tag manager source
expected_outputs: Reusable Toolkit field catalog sourced from CptManager definitions.
Elementor dynamic tag group and tag for Toolkit field keys.
Dynamic tag setting uses key so FieldBindingResolver can parse Elementor serialized bindings.
FilterResolver enriches public post items with Toolkit-managed meta fields that are marked show_in_rest.
Implementation note documents the boundary between field selection, runtime value lookup, and future visual polish.
acceptance_criteria: The dynamic tag is registered on elementor/dynamic_tags/register and does not depend on Elementor Pro internals.
The tag returns the selected sanitized field key, not a decorative label.
Only CptManager definitions are used as the source of Toolkit field options.
Public runtime meta enrichment is limited to public posts and Toolkit meta fields marked show_in_rest.
Existing manual key, plain field binding, and serialized dynamic binding fallbacks remain intact.
No style-control redesign or per-filter visual polish is bundled into this task.
verification: PHP lint passes for changed PHP files.
WP-CLI smoke confirms the Toolkit dynamic tag registers.
WP-CLI smoke confirms a serialized Toolkit dynamic tag resolves through FieldBindingResolver.
WP-CLI smoke confirms public Toolkit meta filters and private Toolkit meta does not.

budgets.complexity_budget: complex but bounded to field-source integration
budgets.context_budget: CPT manager, Elementor integration, dynamic tags API, field resolver, filter runtime
budgets.validation_budget: syntax, schema, composer, WP-CLI smoke, static diff checks

risks: If the tag only lists fields but runtime cannot read values, the integration becomes cosmetic.
If runtime reads arbitrary meta keys, the public filter endpoint could leak behavior about private data.
If dynamic tag parsing changes in Elementor, the existing FieldBindingResolver fallback order must keep manual keys functional.
